# AIChatRender

Read your Claude Code or Codex CLI session in a VS Code panel, with the math
actually rendered. Prose stays plain text; `$$…$$` becomes typeset equations,
updating live as the session runs.

The terminal already shows you the chat. The reason this exists is that LaTeX in
a terminal is unreadable, and copying an equation out of one is worse.

> **Unaffiliated.** AIChatRender is an independent tool. It is not made,
> endorsed, or supported by Anthropic or OpenAI. It reads the session files
> those CLIs already write to your own disk; it uses no API and no account.

## What it does

- **Follows the active session.** Watches this workspace's Claude transcripts
  (`~/.claude/projects/`) and Codex rollouts (`~/.codex/sessions/`), following
  whichever was written most recently and switching automatically. Both vendors
  count a session as this workspace's when its cwd is the workspace folder or
  any directory beneath it, so a CLI started in a subfolder is still followed.
- **AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat** pins the panel to the transcript
  held open by your active terminal's process tree. If the terminal can't be
  matched — an idle CLI often closes its transcript — a picker lists the
  workspace's recent chats.
- **AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick** opens a searchable list of the user
  prompts in the chat being followed, newest first, each shown as its first 80
  characters or so (the cap bounds rendered width, so wide characters count
  double). Picking one scrolls the panel to that turn and flashes it. The
  list covers the messages the panel currently holds, so it never offers a turn
  the panel cannot show.
- **Renders math** with a vendored, pinned KaTeX: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` display,
  `\(…\)` and `$…$` inline. Single-`$` uses Pandoc-style guards so currency and
  `$VAR` don't trigger false positives.
- **Copies equations as LaTeX source**, including when a selection mixes prose
  and formulas, via KaTeX's `copy-tex`.
- **A deliberately small Markdown subset**: headings, lists, blockquotes, rules,
  bold/italic, inline and fenced code. Raw HTML and Markdown links stay inert
  text — see below.
- Shows assistant text and real user prompts, newest 50 messages. Thinking
  blocks, tool calls and results, and harness bookkeeping are skipped.

## Requirements

- **Linux or macOS.** Following the active terminal needs process
  introspection: `/proc` on Linux, `pgrep`/`lsof`/`ps` on macOS.
- **Windows: use WSL or a remote/container workspace.** AIChatRender declares
  `"extensionKind": ["workspace"]`, so it runs on the Linux side of a remote
  window, which is the supported path. Run natively on Windows, the panel and
  manual transcript picking still work, but **Follow Active Terminal Chat**
  reports that it is unsupported rather than silently failing.
- VS Code 1.85 or newer.

## What it reads, and what that means

This is an extension that reads your AI chat transcripts, so it's worth being
precise about the scope.

- **Read-only.** It never writes under `~/.claude/` or `~/.codex/`, and keeps no
  copy, inbox, or history of its own — the panel re-reads the existing
  transcript on load.
- **No network.** No HTTP listener, socket, port, or CDN request. KaTeX is
  vendored and served over VS Code's internal webview channel.
- **Codex discovery reads across projects.** To find the rollout belonging to
  *this* workspace, it must read the **first line** of every rollout in the
  scanned date directories — including ones from your other projects. Those
  lines can contain base instructions, git, and provider metadata. Only `cwd`
  and the session timestamp are retained; metadata from nonmatching rollouts is
  never logged and never reaches the webview. Full contents are read only for
  the one rollout that matches this workspace.
- **Follow Active Terminal Chat** may additionally read the PID-keyed Claude
  state record under `~/.claude/sessions/` and the transcript it names, after
  validating that its real cwd is inside the workspace.
- **No XSS surface.** The Markdown subset builds only fixed DOM elements and
  assigns prose via `textContent`; raw HTML is never parsed. Only math source
  reaches KaTeX (`trust: false`, `throwOnError: false`), under a strict CSP with
  nonce'd scripts, failing soft on malformed records.

The inert-Markdown choice is deliberate. Rendering links or HTML out of a
transcript would turn model output into a clickable surface inside your editor,
which is exactly what this panel is trying not to be.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `AIChatRender: Show Panel` | Open the panel, following the newest transcript. |
| `AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat` | Pin to the active terminal's chat. |
| `AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick` | List the chat's user prompts and scroll to one. |

## Known limitations

- Exactly one workspace folder.
- Automatic discovery does not follow sessions started from a subdirectory, but
  **Follow Active Terminal Chat** can select one whose real cwd is inside the
  workspace.
- No source toggle: with concurrent Claude and Codex sessions, the panel follows
  whichever matching file changed last unless you pin one.
- Codex discovery scans only the last seven date directories, plus tomorrow as a
  cross-time-zone guard. Older rollouts are not followed, even when resumed.
- On macOS, a stale PID-reuse check is weaker than on Linux: `ps` reports
  wall-clock start times that can't be compared to the marker Claude records, so
  AIChatRender verifies the process still exists rather than that it is the *same*
  process.
- These CLIs ship frequently and their session formats are internal and
  undocumented. A format change can break parsing until it's fixed.

## License and citation

MIT — see `LICENSE`. Use it freely, including in commercial work. Bundled KaTeX
is separately MIT-licensed; see `media/katex/LICENSE`.

If AIChatRender is useful in academic work, a citation is appreciated but not
required by the license:

> Chen, Andrew Y. (2026). *AIChatRender: rendered math for AI coding-agent
> transcripts in VS Code.*

content.text:
Fixed. The extension had no table support at all — pipe tables fell through to the paragraph branch and displayed as literal `| a | b |` / `| --- |` lines.

**`media/markdown.js`** — new `table` block in the parser:
- Detects a header row followed by a delimiter row (`| :--- | ---: |`), requiring the column counts to match, per GFM; otherwise the lines stay a paragraph.
- Splits cells on unescaped `|` at the *token* level, so a pipe inside a math span never splits a cell, and `\|` becomes a literal pipe.
- Emits `{type:'table', align, header, rows}` with `'left'|'center'|'right'|''` per column; body rows are padded/truncated to the header width and end at a blank or non-pipe line.

**`media/index.html`** — renders `thead`/`tbody` via a `tableRow` helper using the existing `appendTokens` (so inline code, bold/italic, and KaTeX work in cells), wrapped in an `overflow-x: auto` div. Styling uses VS Code theme vars; cells reset the body's `white-space: pre-wrap` to `normal` so source padding doesn't leak into layout. Alignment goes through `md-align-*` classes, no inline styles, so the CSP is untouched and the no-raw-HTML property holds.

Tests: 3 new cases in `test/markdown.test.js` (alignment + math cell + escaped pipe + short row; mismatched delimiter row; headerless pipe text). Full suite: 69 passing. README and CHANGELOG updated.

I verified the parser against the tests and syntax-checked the panel script, but I have not launched the extension to look at a rendered table — say the word if you want me to run it and screenshot.

"GFM" is GitHub Flavored Markdown, and "pipe table" is the `| a | b |` style specifically. I used both out of habit for precision, but neither earns its keep in a README bullet.

content.text:
Yes — and the empirical answer says that's fine.

**What the patch does and doesn't handle**

Pandoc has four table syntaxes, and "Pandoc tables" isn't one thing:

| Syntax | Result |
|---|---|
| Pipe tables (`\| a \| b \|`) | **Renders** — Pandoc's `pipe_tables` is essentially GFM's, so it's already covered |
| Grid tables (`+---+---+`) | Falls through to a paragraph |
| Simple tables (space-aligned, dash underline) | Paragraph, and the underline hits the pre-existing horizontal-rule regex, so it splits into paragraph/`<hr>`/paragraph |
| Multiline tables | Paragraph |

No false positives — grid tables never trip the detector, because their separator rows use `+` and contain no pipe at all. A Pandoc `: Caption text` line after a table renders as an ordinary paragraph under it, which reads acceptably.

**What the two agents actually emit**

I scanned your synced transcripts in `/workspace/.tools/ai-sesh/data` — 400 sessions (200 newest per vendor), 4,233 assistant messages:

| Vendor | Pipe delimiter rows | Grid | Simple |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Claude Code | 89 (in 33 files) | 0 | 0 |
| Codex | 30 (in 10 files) | 0 | 0 |

Zero grid tables, zero simple tables, across both. Both CLIs emit pipe tables exclusively, which makes sense — it's what their own terminal renderers display, so it's the only syntax that round-trips for them.

So the patch covers 100% of tables observed in your real sessions. Supporting grid or simple tables would be speculative work against a case neither agent has produced in 4,233 messages; I'd skip it. If you want, I'll note the limitation in the README's Markdown-subset bullet so it's documented rather than implied.

One caveat on the numbers: this counts delimiter-row *lines*, so a table with a delimiter row is one hit regardless of its row count, and I sampled the newest 200 files per vendor out of 3,034 rather than reading all 5.5 GB. The direction isn't in doubt, but the absolute counts are a sample.

# Changelog

All notable changes to AIChatRender are documented here.

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Markdown tables render as tables. GFM pipe tables previously had no parser
  rule at all, so a table fell through to the paragraph branch and showed up as
  raw `| --- |` lines. The parser now emits a `table` block with per-column
  alignment from the delimiter row, honours `\|` escapes, and keeps math spans
  intact inside cells; short rows are padded and long rows truncated to the
  header's column count.

### Fixed

- Codex rollouts started in a *subdirectory* of the workspace folder are now
  discovered. Codex matching required the recorded cwd to equal the workspace
  root exactly, while Claude had always accepted any cwd beneath it; a Codex
  session run in, say, `1-SANDBOX/Live,AIChatRender` with `1-SANDBOX` open in
  VS Code was filtered out of the candidate list, so **Follow Active Terminal
  Chat** could not match it even though the terminal held the rollout open, and
  fell back to the picker with only stale chats in it. Both vendors now share
  one realpath-based containment test (`pathWithin`).

## [0.5.0] — 2026-08-02

### Added

- **AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick** (`aichatrender.browseTurns`): a quick
  pick listing the user prompts of the chat being followed, newest first, with
  each prompt previewed to about its first 80 characters and its timestamp as the
  filterable description. Choosing one reveals the panel, scrolls that turn into
  view, and flashes it. Scope is the messages the panel currently retains.
- Messages now carry a monotonic key, sent to the webview and used to address
  the scroll target, so trimming to `MAX_MESSAGES` or a whole-file rebuild
  while the picker is open cannot land the jump on a different message.

### Changed

- Development installs now build a `.vsix` from this repo
  (`scripts/install-local.sh`) instead of copying the source tree into a
  separate staging directory, which had drifted out of sync. `.vscode/launch.json`
  lets F5 load the extension from the repo, so testing a change needs no install
  at all.

# AIChatRender

Read your Claude Code or Codex CLI session in a VS Code panel, with the math
actually rendered. Prose stays plain text; `$$…$$` becomes typeset equations,
updating live as the session runs.

The terminal already shows you the chat. The reason this exists is that LaTeX in
a terminal is unreadable, and copying an equation out of one is worse.

> **Unaffiliated.** AIChatRender is an independent tool. It is not made,
> endorsed, or supported by Anthropic or OpenAI. It reads the session files
> those CLIs already write to your own disk; it uses no API and no account.

## What it does

- **Follows the active session.** Watches this workspace's Claude transcripts
  (`~/.claude/projects/`) and Codex rollouts (`~/.codex/sessions/`), following
  whichever was written most recently and switching automatically. Both vendors
  count a session as this workspace's when its cwd is the workspace folder or
  any directory beneath it, so a CLI started in a subfolder is still followed.
- **AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat** pins the panel to the transcript
  held open by your active terminal's process tree. If the terminal can't be
  matched — an idle CLI often closes its transcript — a picker lists the
  workspace's recent chats.
- **AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick** opens a searchable list of the user
  prompts in the chat being followed, newest first, each shown as its first 80
  characters or so (the cap bounds rendered width, so wide characters count
  double). Picking one scrolls the panel to that turn and flashes it. The
  list covers the messages the panel currently holds, so it never offers a turn
  the panel cannot show.
- **Renders math** with a vendored, pinned KaTeX: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` display,
  `\(…\)` and `$…$` inline. Single-`$` uses Pandoc-style guards so currency and
  `$VAR` don't trigger false positives.
- **Copies equations as LaTeX source**, including when a selection mixes prose
  and formulas, via KaTeX's `copy-tex`.
- **A deliberately small Markdown subset**: headings, lists, blockquotes, rules,
  bold/italic, inline and fenced code, and GFM pipe tables (with column
  alignment and math inside cells). Raw HTML and Markdown links stay inert
  text — see below.
- Shows assistant text and real user prompts, newest 50 messages. Thinking
  blocks, tool calls and results, and harness bookkeeping are skipped.

## Requirements

- **Linux or macOS.** Following the active terminal needs process
  introspection: `/proc` on Linux, `pgrep`/`lsof`/`ps` on macOS.
- **Windows: use WSL or a remote/container workspace.** AIChatRender declares
  `"extensionKind": ["workspace"]`, so it runs on the Linux side of a remote
  window, which is the supported path. Run natively on Windows, the panel and
  manual transcript picking still work, but **Follow Active Terminal Chat**
  reports that it is unsupported rather than silently failing.
- VS Code 1.85 or newer.

## What it reads, and what that means

This is an extension that reads your AI chat transcripts, so it's worth being
precise about the scope.

- **Read-only.** It never writes under `~/.claude/` or `~/.codex/`, and keeps no
  copy, inbox, or history of its own — the panel re-reads the existing
  transcript on load.
- **No network.** No HTTP listener, socket, port, or CDN request. KaTeX is
  vendored and served over VS Code's internal webview channel.
- **Codex discovery reads across projects.** To find the rollout belonging to
  *this* workspace, it must read the **first line** of every rollout in the
  scanned date directories — including ones from your other projects. Those
  lines can contain base instructions, git, and provider metadata. Only `cwd`
  and the session timestamp are retained; metadata from nonmatching rollouts is
  never logged and never reaches the webview. Full contents are read only for
  the one rollout that matches this workspace.
- **Follow Active Terminal Chat** may additionally read the PID-keyed Claude
  state record under `~/.claude/sessions/` and the transcript it names, after
  validating that its real cwd is inside the workspace.
- **No XSS surface.** The Markdown subset builds only fixed DOM elements and
  assigns prose via `textContent`; raw HTML is never parsed. Only math source
  reaches KaTeX (`trust: false`, `throwOnError: false`), under a strict CSP with
  nonce'd scripts, failing soft on malformed records.

The inert-Markdown choice is deliberate. Rendering links or HTML out of a
transcript would turn model output into a clickable surface inside your editor,
which is exactly what this panel is trying not to be.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `AIChatRender: Show Panel` | Open the panel, following the newest transcript. |
| `AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat` | Pin to the active terminal's chat. |
| `AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick` | List the chat's user prompts and scroll to one. |

## Known limitations

- Exactly one workspace folder.
- Automatic discovery does not follow sessions started from a subdirectory, but
  **Follow Active Terminal Chat** can select one whose real cwd is inside the
  workspace.
- No source toggle: with concurrent Claude and Codex sessions, the panel follows
  whichever matching file changed last unless you pin one.
- Codex discovery scans only the last seven date directories, plus tomorrow as a
  cross-time-zone guard. Older rollouts are not followed, even when resumed.
- On macOS, a stale PID-reuse check is weaker than on Linux: `ps` reports
  wall-clock start times that can't be compared to the marker Claude records, so
  AIChatRender verifies the process still exists rather than that it is the *same*
  process.
- These CLIs ship frequently and their session formats are internal and
  undocumented. A format change can break parsing until it's fixed.

## License and citation

MIT — see `LICENSE`. Use it freely, including in commercial work. Bundled KaTeX
is separately MIT-licensed; see `media/katex/LICENSE`.

If AIChatRender is useful in academic work, a citation is appreciated but not
required by the license:

> transcripts in VS Code.*

# AIChatRender

Read your Claude Code or Codex CLI session in a VS Code panel, with the math
actually rendered. Prose stays plain text; `$$…$$` becomes typeset equations,
updating live as the session runs.

The terminal already shows you the chat. The reason this exists is that LaTeX in
a terminal is unreadable, and copying an equation out of one is worse.

> **Unaffiliated.** AIChatRender is an independent tool. It is not made,
> endorsed, or supported by Anthropic or OpenAI. It reads the session files
> those CLIs already write to your own disk; it uses no API and no account.

## What it does

- **Follows the active session.** Watches this workspace's Claude transcripts
  (`~/.claude/projects/`) and Codex rollouts (`~/.codex/sessions/`), following
  whichever was written most recently and switching automatically. Both vendors
  count a session as this workspace's when its cwd is the workspace folder or
  any directory beneath it, so a CLI started in a subfolder is still followed.
- **AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat** pins the panel to the transcript
  held open by your active terminal's process tree. If the terminal can't be
  matched — an idle CLI often closes its transcript — a picker lists the
  workspace's recent chats.
- **AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick** opens a searchable list of the user
  prompts in the chat being followed, newest first, each shown as its first 80
  characters or so (the cap bounds rendered width, so wide characters count
  double). Picking one scrolls the panel to that turn and flashes it. The
  list covers the messages the panel currently holds, so it never offers a turn
  the panel cannot show.
- **Renders math** with a vendored, pinned KaTeX: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` display,
  `\(…\)` and `$…$` inline. Single-`$` uses Pandoc-style guards so currency and
  `$VAR` don't trigger false positives.
- **Copies equations as LaTeX source**, including when a selection mixes prose
  and formulas, via KaTeX's `copy-tex`.
- **A deliberately small Markdown subset**: headings, lists, blockquotes, rules,
  bold/italic, inline and fenced code, and `| a | b |` tables (with column
  alignment and math inside cells). Raw HTML and Markdown links stay inert
  text — see below.
- Shows assistant text and real user prompts, newest 50 messages. Thinking
  blocks, tool calls and results, and harness bookkeeping are skipped.

## Requirements

- **Linux or macOS.** Following the active terminal needs process
  introspection: `/proc` on Linux, `pgrep`/`lsof`/`ps` on macOS.
- **Windows: use WSL or a remote/container workspace.** AIChatRender declares
  `"extensionKind": ["workspace"]`, so it runs on the Linux side of a remote
  window, which is the supported path. Run natively on Windows, the panel and
  manual transcript picking still work, but **Follow Active Terminal Chat**
  reports that it is unsupported rather than silently failing.
- VS Code 1.85 or newer.

## What it reads, and what that means

This is an extension that reads your AI chat transcripts, so it's worth being
precise about the scope.

- **Read-only.** It never writes under `~/.claude/` or `~/.codex/`, and keeps no
  copy, inbox, or history of its own — the panel re-reads the existing
  transcript on load.
- **No network.** No HTTP listener, socket, port, or CDN request. KaTeX is
  vendored and served over VS Code's internal webview channel.
- **Codex discovery reads across projects.** To find the rollout belonging to
  *this* workspace, it must read the **first line** of every rollout in the
  scanned date directories — including ones from your other projects. Those
  lines can contain base instructions, git, and provider metadata. Only `cwd`
  and the session timestamp are retained; metadata from nonmatching rollouts is
  never logged and never reaches the webview. Full contents are read only for
  the one rollout that matches this workspace.
- **Follow Active Terminal Chat** may additionally read the PID-keyed Claude
  state record under `~/.claude/sessions/` and the transcript it names, after
  validating that its real cwd is inside the workspace.
- **No XSS surface.** The Markdown subset builds only fixed DOM elements and
  assigns prose via `textContent`; raw HTML is never parsed. Only math source
  reaches KaTeX (`trust: false`, `throwOnError: false`), under a strict CSP with
  nonce'd scripts, failing soft on malformed records.

The inert-Markdown choice is deliberate. Rendering links or HTML out of a
transcript would turn model output into a clickable surface inside your editor,
which is exactly what this panel is trying not to be.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `AIChatRender: Show Panel` | Open the panel, following the newest transcript. |
| `AIChatRender: Follow Active Terminal Chat` | Pin to the active terminal's chat. |
| `AIChatRender: Browse Turns and Pick` | List the chat's user prompts and scroll to one. |

## Known limitations

- Exactly one workspace folder.
- Automatic discovery does not follow sessions started from a subdirectory, but
  **Follow Active Terminal Chat** can select one whose real cwd is inside the
  workspace.
- No source toggle: with concurrent Claude and Codex sessions, the panel follows
  whichever matching file changed last unless you pin one.
- Codex discovery scans only the last seven date directories, plus tomorrow as a
  cross-time-zone guard. Older rollouts are not followed, even when resumed.
- On macOS, a stale PID-reuse check is weaker than on Linux: `ps` reports
  wall-clock start times that can't be compared to the marker Claude records, so
  AIChatRender verifies the process still exists rather than that it is the *same*
  process.
- These CLIs ship frequently and their session formats are internal and
  undocumented. A format change can break parsing until it's fixed.

## License and citation

MIT — see `LICENSE`. Use it freely, including in commercial work. Bundled KaTeX
is separately MIT-licensed; see `media/katex/LICENSE`.

If AIChatRender is useful in academic work, a citation is appreciated but not
required by the license:

> Chen, Andrew Y. (2026). *AIChatRender: rendered math for AI coding-agent
> transcripts in VS Code.*
